answers.answer: SQLite is a database engine embedded in client applications through its public C library interface. The repository also builds the sqlite3 command-line shell and Tcl bindings/testfixture, which call the library. External application callers are not enumerated by this repository.

Principal components: public API (sqlite.h.in); SQL parser (parse.y/Lemon); query planning/code generation (where*.c); prepared-statement virtual machine (vdbe.c); B-tree storage (btree.c); transaction pager (pager.c); OS access through pluggable VFS (os_unix.c/os_win.c). Shell and Tcl bindings are separate clients; ext/ contains optional extensions.

Core implementation is C, with a generated Lemon parser and generated sqlite3.h/amalgamation. Unix builds use Autosetup configure plus make; Windows supports MSVC/nmake Makefile.msc. Tcl drives generation/testing. Public sqlite3.h separates application API from unstable internal headers; shell/Tcl are outside core. The map also inventories Java/JNI and JavaScript/WASM, but its C extraction is file-only.

The selected library entry is sqlite3_exec(db, SQL, callback, callbackArgument, errorOutput), declared in sqlite.h.in and implemented in src/legacy.c. It requires an already-open connection; this is not a CLI main entry.

src/legacy.c implements sqlite3_exec: prepare each statement, step it, collect column names/text, invoke xCallback, finalize, and continue at the leftover SQL. The API specifies one callback per result row, NULL pointers for SQL NULL, and SQLITE_ABORT on a nonzero callback return; callback arrays are valid only during the callback.

Direct dependencies visible in sqlite3_exec: sqlite3_prepare_v2; sqlite3_step; sqlite3_column_count/name/text/type; sqlite3VdbeFinalize; connection mutex enter/leave; sqlite3SafetyCheckOk; sqlite3Error; allocation/free/string duplication; sqlite3OomFault; sqlite3ApiExit; sqlite3_errmsg; whitespace classification. xCallback is a supplied function pointer, not a statically resolved internal callee. Parser, planner, B-tree and pager are downstream, not direct calls from this function.

Supported source path: sqlite3_exec -> sqlite3_prepare_v2 -> sqlite3LockAndPrepare -> sqlite3Prepare -> sqlite3RunParser -> generated sqlite3Parser. SELECT grammar dispatches sqlite3Select with SRT_Output. Execution proceeds sqlite3_step -> sqlite3Step -> sqlite3VdbeExec; OP_ResultRow exposes values and returns SQLITE_ROW; exec then invokes xCallback. The callback target is supplied at runtime. SQL/schema/compiled options determine the generated program and storage path; this is source-supported control flow, not an observed runtime trace.

sqlite3_get_table in src/table.c directly calls sqlite3_exec with sqlite3_get_table_cb and a TabResult accumulator. Its callback copies column names and row strings/NULLs, counts rows, and returns nonzero on incompatible column counts or allocation failure. Therefore changing row delivery, value representation, column-name delivery, or abort handling can affect this consumer (when SQLITE_OMIT_GET_TABLE is not enabled).

test/exec.test contains exec-1.2 (comments/empty statements around SELECT) and exec-1.3 (SELECT after a second connection changes schema), both expecting status 0 plus column names and row values. Tcl command sqlite3_exec is registered to test_exec in src/test1.c; test_exec calls the C sqlite3_exec with exec_printf_cb, which appends names and values to a Tcl_DString. These are inspected tests, not executed tests; coverage enumeration is not exhaustive.

SQL enters sqlite3_exec as zSql. It passes zSql and &zLeftover to prepare_v2. Through LockAndPrepare/Prepare, RunParser tokenizes with sqlite3GetToken, passes tokens to sqlite3Parser, advances the input pointer, and records Parse.zTail. Prepare publishes that tail through pzTail and returns pVdbe as sqlite3_stmt; v2 also saves consumed SQL. For bounded nonterminated input, Prepare copies SQL and rebases the tail to the original buffer. Exec advances to zLeftover, skips whitespace, and repeats.
